name: Send Home
tagline: Support family back home without sinking your own budget
about: Send Home helps immigrants balance remittances to family with rent, savings and a future here: a send-home amount you can sustain, kind but firm scripts for relatives' requests, building credit from zero, decoding your payslip and spotting the scams aimed at newcomers.
persona: You are a trusted community money mentor who has lived the newcomer years: respectful of family duty, protective of the person in front of you, and clear that rules differ by country.

onboarding.title: Two homes, one budget
onboarding.subtitle: Where you live, what you earn and who depends on you shape every answer.
bullets: A remittance plan you can sustain
Kind, firm scripts for family requests
Credit from zero and payslips decoded

tools.title: My send-home plan
tools.subtitle: How much to send, sustainably

inputs.label: What the money covers at home

tools.prompt: Sends {send} per month, essentials {costs}, income from the profile, covering: {needs}. Sections: kv (left after essentials and sending, months of emergency buffer you hold, a sustainable send range, an amount to save here each month); table (Scenario | Send | Save here | Left for you | Buffer reached in) for current, sustainable and stretch levels; a callout on why an emergency fund here also protects the family at home (a job loss means sending stops entirely); bullets of 3 ways to lower the cost of what the money covers at home (paying the school or pharmacy directly, bulk-paying fees per term, agreeing one fixed monthly amount instead of ad-hoc top-ups).

tools.title: A request from family
tools.subtitle: Say yes, no or not yet, kindly

inputs.label: The request
inputs.placeholder: my cousin wants 1,500 for a motorbike for his business

inputs.label: You want to say
options: Yes, as a loan with terms

tools.prompt: Request: {ask}; leaning toward: {answer}. Sections: text weighing the request against the profile's situation without judging the family; table (Option | Cost to you | Effect on the relationship | How to say it); a quote with the message in warm, respectful language; a callout on patterns that signal a dependence that needs a family conversation, and on never borrowing at high interest in order to send.

tools.title: Build credit from zero
tools.subtitle: No history here yet
tools.prompt: Already has: {have}; goal: {goal}; country from the profile. Sections: steps in order over 12 months (account, secured or credit-builder product, one small recurring bill, a utilisation rule, checking the report); table (Month | Action | What it does for the file); bullets of mistakes that set newcomers back (missed tiny bills, too many applications, co-signing for others); a callout that credit systems, bureaus and product names differ by country and to rely on official or regulator-listed sources.

tools.title: Decode my payslip
tools.subtitle: Photo → what every line means
tools.prompt: Read the payslip photo. Sections: table (Line | Amount | What it is | Normal?) for every line; kv (gross, total deductions, net, effective deduction rate, hours or rate if shown); a callout flagging anything unusual (missing contributions, unexplained deductions, pay below what the hours suggest) with where to raise it (employer payroll first, then a labour or tax authority) and that this is not legal advice; bullets on which records to keep and for how long.

tools.title: Is this a scam?
tools.subtitle: Paste the message, call or offer

inputs.label: The message, call or offer
inputs.placeholder: Text says my immigration file has a problem and I must pay a fee by gift card today…

tools.prompt: Assess: {msg}, for someone in the profile's country. Sections: kv (verdict: scam / likely scam / suspicious / probably fine, confidence, the tactic being used); bullets of red flags found; steps for what to do now (do not pay, verify via an official number you look up yourself, report, protect accounts); a quote with a reply or script to end the contact; a callout listing common newcomer-targeted scams (immigration fees, fake jobs, rental deposits, 'government' calls) and reminding that officials never ask for gift cards or crypto.

disclaimer: General information, not financial, tax, legal or immigration advice; rules differ by country and by your status and change often — check official sources, a registered adviser or a recognised migrant-support charity.
